items.title: Constantinople in 1197
items.text: Around 1197 the city stands at the edge of ruin, threatening to drag the Dream down with it.

items.title: Time-Motion Managers (first edition)
items.text: The mechanical clock began with Benedictine monks around 1200 to time prayers; some say it also served Time magick.

items.title: The Latin Empire
items.text: The crusaders took Byzantium in 1204 and set up a feudal Latin Empire, also called Romania, with the emperor above vassals such as the King of Thessalonica and the Prince of Achaia.

items.title: The Latin Empire
items.text: The Toreador Methuselah Michael, the Patriarch of Constantinople, met Final Death in 1204, but that influence lingers.

items.title: Constantinople after the Dream
items.text: Ghouls abandoned when the Trinity families burned or fled in 1204 now hunt Cainites from the Grand Bazaar.

items.title: The Heretical end times
items.text: Most Heretics expect the Third Caine to appear in 1206 and dwell on earth for thirty-three years, like Christ.

items.title: Haunted places of the Isles
items.text: Bramber Castle in Sussex is said to hold the ghosts of three de Braose children starved by King John and of Lady Maud de Hurst, murdered in 1210.

items.title: Fall of Mistridge
items.text: The Hermetic sanctum at Mistridge fell in 1210, brought down by mortals led by a group calling itself the Craftmasons.

items.title: Gunpowder and siege
items.text: Mages have already used magic to build such weapons, and several cannon were fired in the destruction of the Mistridge Covenant in 1210.

items.title: Road to the Council
items.text: The Craftmasons destroyed Mistridge in the winter of 1210, and the Convention of the White Tower met on 25 March 1325.

ruling.note: Start of the Ascension War: The Fragile Path (2nd) counts it from 1330, while Sorcerers Crusade (Revised) and the NPC rivalry rules open it at Mistridge in 1210. 1210 stands; the 1330 clause is cut.

items.title: Masters the Artisans honour
items.text: Roger Bacon's influence among the High Artisans remains immense; the Craftmasons showed their strength in 1210 when they brought down Mistridge with cannon.

items.title: The Holy Roman Empire in 1230
items.text: A moderate Ventrue faction, the Antasians, watched over the crowning of Frederick II at Frankfurt in 1212.

items.title: The Holy Roman Empire in 1230
items.text: After the Children's Crusade of 1212, Giselher, Ventrue prince of Cologne, barred Clan Lasombra from the city. Giselher never proved the Magisters were behind it, but used the charge against rivals anyway.

items.title: The Balm of Gilead
items.text: Before 1215 the vial was widely believed to have reached Cistercian monks near the start of the 12th century, though how it got there is unclear.

items.title: Marc de Brabant
items.text: Given as a child to a Benedictine priory in the twelfth century, Marc ran away at sixteen and was Embraced in 1216 by Megan of Bristol, a Gangrel of the 10th Generation.

items.title: Eye for the Weakness of Steel
items.text: It began among the Fellowship of Our Lady, a company of Toreador and Ventrue, and it passed to their successors after the Fellowship broke apart in 1218 through infighting.

items.title: France in 1230
items.text: Paris is the seat of the joint Toreador and Ventrue Grand Court. Geoffrey, a Ventrue, has led it as Prince of Paris since 1222, after overthrowing Alexander, Geoffrey's own sire.

items.title: Catherine Maidstone
items.text: A Toreador of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1229 by Maiselle of Rochester, born in the village of Strood.

items.title: Camilla and Cretheus
items.text: Cretheus, Fifth Generation Ventrue and childe of Mithras, ruled Rome in fact for nearly 300 years and is the only public member of the Ignoti; bending the knee to Camilla in 1229 was read as the hidden ones' blessing.

items.title: The Oath-Truce
items.text: It began in AD 1130 and so will end around 1230.

items.title: Mages of the Dark Medieval
items.text: In 1230 common superstition supports belief in magic, which helps mages cast with impunity; only in later ages does belief turn against them.

items.title: The great killers
items.text: A few great diseases cause most deaths in 1230; some can empty a village in weeks, others leave victims wasted husks.

items.title: The Eclipse of 1230
items.text: In May of 1230 an eclipse darkens the sky so deeply that workers go home thinking night has come.

items.title: The Ten Tribes
items.text: The Garou of 1230 count Ten Tribes.

items.title: The Anda
items.text: They see this era as a time to feed on the spreading chaos and fear and to prepare for the Golden Horde, which turns west in 1235 and pulls back in 1242.

items.title: The Heretical end times
items.text: Counting from a creation date of 3761 B.C.E. and five stages of a thousand years each, Heretics expect the material world to end in 1239.

items.title: Garou and the Tatar Yoke
items.text: With Kin of their own among the Mongol clans, the Shadow Lords quietly backed the Tatar Yoke over Russia from about 1240 to 1480.

items.title: Dark Medieval Italy
items.text: By the 1240s Italy is only a name on the map; loyalty comes from the cities, swollen by migrants from the countryside.

items.title: Kupala's Eve and the Tzimisce revolt
items.text: The Mongol invasion of 1241 broke Tzimisce holdings in the east and nearly destroyed the elder known as the Butcher of Rus. Elders tightened their grip on their thralls in response.

items.title: Scáth, the Wandering City
items.text: A diary of 1242 tells of a coterie sent by an unnamed powerful patron, chasing clues through Dublin, Edinburgh and Norwich toward London.
items.ref: Tome of Secrets p. 9 (pdf 10); Tome of Secrets p. 10 (pdf 11)

items.title: The Order of Saint Lazarus
items.text: Most of its men-at-arms die at Gaza in 1244, and its time in the Holy Land is ending during the 13th century.

items.title: Nasch the Circassian
items.text: A Ventrue of the 7th Generation, Embraced in 1263 by Palamon the Copt; a few childhood memories of the mountains are all that remain from before Egypt.

items.title: Medieval schisms
items.text: Roger Bacon's London Accord of 1268 ended the war among England's artisan guilds; de Varre founded the Solificati in 1315, and they broke away from the Order of Reason in 1335.

items.title: The Hospitallers and the Teutonic Knights
items.text: Large endowments in Western Europe fund the Hospitallers' work in the East, a structure that lets the order outlast the loss of the Holy Land in 1291.

items.title: The Striders in the Crusades
items.text: Around 1300 the wandering Caern of Long Voyages was thrown into an attack on a Zmei's servants in southern Russia and lost with its whole sept.

items.title: Raise the Sun
items.text: The last reliable account dates to about 1300, back when the tribe still kept its alliance with Helios and the Mound Builder Dreamspeakers.

items.title: The Treaty of the Quincunx
items.text: In 1304, ten years after Kublai Khan died, ancestors from three courts (Yellow Emperor, White Tiger and Black Tortoise) met at the Shaolin monastery near Changan and signed the Treaty of the Quincunx.

items.title: The fall of the Temple, 1307
items.text: King Philip the Fair had the French Templars seized in 1307 on heresy charges, with papal leave, and is widely thought to have wanted their wealth.

items.title: Templars as a Craft
items.text: In 1307 Philip the Fair had the French Templars arrested for heresy; some say vampire advisors or Batini with grudges pushed the king.

items.title: The Way of the Ancient Lawgivers
items.text: Founded in 1312, it holds that all Kindred must return to the ways of the First City, when mortals and lesser vampires honoured the Antediluvians.

items.title: The Chodona
items.text: Ten years on they wrote that purpose down as the Chodona, the Wheel of the Law with eight spokes; by 1314 the Wheel stretched from Nepal to Ireland.

items.title: Baerwald
items.text: Pagans gathered there as a refuge from persecution, and in 1317 Sir Garland declared the land a fief named Baerwald, an open insult to Rome and the Empire.

items.title: Chaoticians
items.text: In 1325, as that Order formally began, mathematicians made a sub-lodge, the Arithmeticians, never strong enough to be a Convention.

items.title: Vincent Day
items.text: A Ventrue antitribu of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1327 by Leander Phipps, once a Templar in the Crusades.

items.title: Medieval schisms
items.text: The Paris University Purge of 1330 killed many mages and destroyed the Hermetic covenant of Le Ictus.

items.title: War of the Dust Witch
items.text: The War of the Dust Witch near Great Zimbabwe, 1345 to 1350, split the Ngoma and the Madzimbabwe into separate groups; plague in 1420 set them at war, each blaming the other.

items.title: The Black Death and the Second Great Maelstrom
items.text: Plague reaches Europe. The dead cross the Shroud in such numbers that the Second Great Maelstrom breaks over the Underworld.

items.title: The Shattering
items.text: Banality closes the ways to Arcadia. The last open trods fail and the fae who stay must hide in mortal bodies.

items.title: Roderigo al-Dakhil
items.text: Once a Castilian soldier fighting to retake Cadiz, Roderigo was Embraced in 1354 by Mokhadaji Ranpur, a Nagaraja of the 6th Generation.

items.title: War of the Dust Witch
items.text: The Screaming Ghost Purge of 1356 to 1360 set Dalou'laoshi and Wu Lung against the Akashics and drove the Brotherhood back into Tibet.

items.title: The Convention of Thorns
items.text: Brujah signed twice, since clan members sat on both sides of the table. Most European Kindred active when the revolt began in 1381 were dead by its end in 1493.

items.title: Knights of St. George
items.text: The Resolute Knights of St. George were founded in Syria in the 11th century and by the 1400s had houses from Ireland to India.

items.title: Mukhtar Bey
items.text: Mukhtar Bey has held the domain since first claiming it in 1406.

items.title: The Camarilla is formed
items.text: Elders of several clans bind themselves into one sect to hide the Kindred from the Inquisition.
items.ref: V20 Lore of the Clans pdf 251

ruling.note: Kept at 1435 (V20 Lore of the Clans). A Guide to the Anarchs counts the Camarilla from 1486, the first Conclave (ev-first-conclave); V20 reads 1435 as the founding and 1486 as the first Conclave, so both cards stand.

items.title: Lady Nightshade
items.text: Lady Nightshade's story begins in Harrogate, England, at Midsummer of 1435.

items.title: Road to the Council
items.text: In 1440 the Hermetic master Baldric met Lady Nightshade of the Verbena and Master Valorian of the Chorus in the ruins of Mistridge, where fae are said to have visited them, and the three agreed to found an order.

items.title: The fall of the Cappadocians
items.text: Augustus Giovanni diablerizes Cappadocius. The Giovanni set out to destroy what is left of the clan.

items.title: Augustus and the Promise of 1528
items.text: Augustus Giovanni diablerized the Cappadocian founder in 1444, rising to the Third Generation and splitting the old clan from the Venetian family.

items.title: The Premascines
items.text: Giovanni tell of kin who helped Augustus rise against the founder, Embraced before 1444, and so perhaps of the Fourth or Fifth Generation. Accounts give anywhere from four to twelve of them.

items.title: The founding wars
items.text: Daedalean forces took Doissetep in 1448; the physical fortress fell and the main keep moved to a Horizon Realm.

items.title: The founding wars
items.text: The Second Mistridge Convocation in 1449 came under attack by Craftmasons and Artificers; the mystics won at heavy cost and helped build Horizon afterward.

items.title: The making of Horizon
items.text: After the defeat of the Craftmasons in the Battle of Flames in 1450, the Primi of the Traditions resolved to build a Realm far from Earth as their meeting place.

items.title: The founding wars
items.text: Tezghul the Insane and Lithuanian demon-worshippers ravaged the Baltic from Kupala Alka from 1450 to 1453, and in 1452 the Daedaleans swore an Oath of Fire against vampires and magi.

items.title: The making of Horizon
items.text: At a minor Tribunal in the Gediz Caves in 1452 the Nodes, still called the Columns of Power, were formally dedicated; among them were Stonehenge and Glastonbury Tor.

items.title: The Servitors of Irad
items.text: Founded in 1456, the cult recruits no one openly and works to keep other Kindred weak and misled before Gehenna.

items.title: France in the Age of Masks
items.text: Louis XI takes the throne in 1461 and drags France into plots and near revolt; Charles VIII invades Italy to claim Naples, starting some 50 years of war that wins nothing lasting.

items.title: The Grand Convocation ends
items.text: After nine years of talks the mystic mages found the Council of Nine Traditions against the Order of Reason.

items.title: Parovich
items.text: A Nosferatu antitribu of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1467 by Boronisk, once an officer in the army of Ivan the Great.

items.title: The first Camarilla Conclave
items.text: The sect holds its first Conclave and names its first Justicars.
items.ref: V20 Lore of the Clans pdf 251

items.title: The Convention of Thorns
items.text: The Anarch Revolt ends at Thorns. The anarchs who refuse the treaty go on to found the Sabbat; the Assamites are cursed.
items.ref: V20 Lore of the Clans pdf 251

items.title: The Eldest and the du'at
items.text: Jamal, a warrior, held the Black Throne from 1494 to 1998. Ur-Shulgi says Jamal refused to renounce Allah and was destroyed for it; many schismatics call Jamal a martyr. Ur-Shulgi does not take the title, giving it to Haqim alone.

items.title: Hong Kong by Night
items.text: For about 1500 years Hong Kong was a backwater ruled from Canton, its villages farming and fishing while Canton grew into a great trading city.

items.title: Voragg the Unbound
items.text: Voragg has served the Wyrm for centuries, mostly while bound in a rock deep under the Rocky Mountains, where a Wendigo tribe sealed it after it troubled them in the late 1500s.

items.title: The Aztec Empire before Cortes
items.text: By 1519 more than forty conquered provinces paid tribute to the emperor, who would soon need a Flower War, a battle fought only to take captives for sacrifice, if no new states could be found to conquer.

items.title: Augustus and the Promise of 1528
items.text: Within decades other clans called the Necromancers Devil Kindred. To avoid a united front against them, the Giovanni swore in 1528 to stay forever outside Kindred affairs.

items.title: The Patmostine Order
items.text: It was founded in the 1530s, in the wake of the Reformation, by the French Toreador Louvel Tarneau.

items.title: Black Hand Ranks and Marks
items.text: The crescent tattoo of the Hand has been in use since at least about 1550.

items.title: The Twilight Cult
items.text: Founded in 1550, it believes a single Book of Nod stanza about the last daughter of Eve is the key: control or destroy that daughter and Gehenna is averted.

items.title: Seats won and lost
items.text: During the witch-hunts of the 1560s refugees flooded Horizon, and Doissetep, once called its sister Chantry, broke with it over a failed plan for European universities.

items.title: France in the Age of Masks
items.text: Catherine di Medici rules as regent for the young kings from 1560 to 1589, and the strife between Catholic nobles and Huguenots peaks in the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre of 1572.

items.title: Cockatrice
items.text: The last mortal record of one is a Warsaw church entry from 1587. Survivors now lurk in rural Chantries and unsettled Realms, where they plague mages in their sanctuaries.
items.ref: Bygone Bestiary p. 18 (pdf 20); Bygone Bestiary p. 19 (pdf 21)

items.title: The Croatan give themselves at Roanoke
items.text: The whole tribe dies to stop a great servant of the Wyrm. No living Croatan remains.

items.title: The Third Great Maelstrom
items.text: After the Looting, the Breaking of the Guilds and the Flaying of Obsidian, the worst storm yet cuts Stygia off. The Shroud thickens.

items.title: Polonia
items.text: Polonia is of the 7th generation, Embraced in 1600 by Anton de Concepcion.

items.title: Justicars
items.text: Archons, the justicars' agents, are usually picked from promising ancillae and young elders. They existed long before the title, which came into use in the late 1600s, probably from the Brujah.

items.title: The Sabbat of Ville-Marie
items.text: By the middle of the 1600s, tales of torture and of children shaped into living mounds of bone and flesh reached Camarilla ears in France. The Toreador investigated, found signs of unsanctioned emigration, and put pawns in key posts to take hold of the colony.

items.title: Raymond Narcisse
items.text: Once Father Raymond, a convert born in the West Indies, recruited from a Norman monastery for Pierre de l'Ancre's witch hunts in Labourd in the early 1600s.

items.title: Maryann Fletcher
items.text: A Nosferatu of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1614 by Stanford Warwick, who found Maryann burned yet alive in a tavern after a Ventrue purge of the sire's servants.

items.title: Jeremy MacNeil
items.text: Jeremy MacNeil is a Brujah of the Eighth Generation, born in 1631 and Embraced in 1657.

items.title: The blood gods of Tenochtitlan
items.text: During an eclipse on 23 August 1691, tendrils of shadow impaled Lasombra in their crypts, and three died. Goratrix and the Tremere antitribu later claimed to have destroyed Tezcatlipoca with a ritual using the black ichor from the wounds; they showed no proof, but Tezcatlipoca was never seen again.

items.title: The Aztec Fiends
items.text: Through the 1700s the Lasombra and Tzimisce fought a war of pawns inside the colonial Church, Lasombra backing Spanish-born priests and the Tzimisce stirring up creole ones, until armed priests clashed and the army stepped in.

items.title: The Hippocratic Circle's long past
items.text: Racism and sexism took hold in the Circle in the 1700s, demeaning its women and its non-European forebears, now called the Aesculapians.

items.title: Doran
items.text: Doran crossed to North America and in the early 1700s went south rather than north to Canada, settling in the Louisiana territory.

items.title: The Taking of California
items.text: Ever since Spanish monks came early in the 1700s, Old World undead have ruled the New World's mortals by murder and deceit, hidden behind the Masquerade.

items.title: Simon de Cosa
items.text: Cosa attacked Doran in 1713, and for years their mortal followers clashed. Cosa had Bienville removed from office and a servant of Cosa's own, Antoine Cadillac, made governor.

items.title: The Hippocratic Circle's long past
items.text: Life-extension work let leading Technocrats live for centuries; Reginald Proctor, extended in 1715, was the only one lost before the Anomaly, by suicide in 1914.

items.title: Edgardo Robbia
items.text: A Brujah of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1736 by Katherine Wiese, who released Edgardo early in the nineteenth century.

items.title: Doran
items.text: Early in a long war with the Brujah Simon de Cosa, Doran made the governor, Bienville, a ghoul. In 1743 Bienville broke free with a mage's help and returned to Europe.
items.ref: New Orleans by Night p. 18 (pdf 19); New Orleans by Night p. 19 (pdf 20)

items.title: The bayou treaty
items.text: Werewolves followed their Cajun kinfolk to the bayous after 1755 and fought the Uktena already there over a caern. In the end the vampires and the Uktena together pushed Cosa into the western swamps.
items.ref: New Orleans by Night p. 19 (pdf 20); New Orleans by Night p. 20 (pdf 21)

items.title: Mage history from 1756
items.text: In 1756 more than a hundred Native American Dreamspeakers left Horizon over bias against tribal and shamanic magic.

items.title: Cock Robin
items.text: Robin was a silversmith's apprentice in colonial America, Embraced in 1757 during the French and English war for the continent and then abandoned by the sire.
items.ref: Children of the Night p. 45 (pdf 45); Children of the Night p. 46 (pdf 46)

items.title: Simon de Cosa
items.text: Idealist elders in Spain who hoped to settle in Louisiana had France cede the territory to Spain in 1763. Doran's servants lost their offices, and Cosa rose again and drove the Ventrue from the city.

items.title: Tatiana Stepanova
items.text: A Ravnos of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1764 by Vasily Vasilevich, born to a noble family.

items.title: The Josians
items.text: The Inner Circle founded the order at its 1764 gathering, when the Hellfire Clubs were in fashion; rumour credits Meerlinda with the name.

items.title: Germaine
items.text: When Louis XVI took the throne in 1774, the Toreador of the French court backed the status quo against reform.

items.title: The Gumagan
items.text: Gumagan live in the deserts, Arnhem Land, New Guinea and the Torres Strait Islands; none have been left in southern Australia since the war that began in 1788.

items.title: Laurette Morel
items.text: A Toreador of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1790 by Émeric de Sauveterre, at home on the Côte d'Azur among the very rich; Villon sees a former Anarch self in Laurette.

items.title: Stargazers of Australia
items.text: Luther Gazes-Inward, the first Stargazer in Australia, landed at Sydney Town in 1790, and the tribe hoped to learn from the Aboriginal peoples and the Bunyip, who would not speak with them.

items.title: House Genji
items.text: They took the name of the first Genji, vampires who had driven out the Bishamon centuries before, and their power grew with Japan's rise in the late 1800s and early 1900s.

items.title: The New World Order's rise
items.text: Its power grew through the 1800s as it infiltrated groups, among them the first mixed Tradition Chantries, and it became the Technocracy's internal police.

items.title: Chaoticians
items.text: In the 1800s they joined others around the computer to become the Difference Engineers, finally finding a place in the Union.

items.title: Ayisha Jocastian
items.text: A Turkish Cypriot born under Ottoman rule in the 1800s and among the best-known vampires of the modern era.

items.title: Bone Gnawer Kin in Other Lines
items.text: By the late 1800s the tribe had Kin among Irish and Scottish families, and descendants who earned glory were often taken in by the Fianna, so many Garou carry a Bone Gnawer ancestor they would rather hide.

items.title: Brujah of the West
items.text: The western Brujah are younger than most clans of the Camarilla; those Embraced in the 1800s barely know the old tragedies of their line.

items.title: Andrew Seneca
items.text: Born a slave on a Georgia cotton plantation and taken into the house as manservant to Jackson Mills; Embraced in 1807 by Monica San Valentin, Ventrue of the 8th Generation.

items.title: Esperanza Lucifer
items.text: Lasombra of the 5th Generation, Embraced in 1812 by one known as Mary; when one Esperanza Lucifer falls, a new one takes up the fearsome role.

items.title: Mage history from 1756
items.text: The Seers of Chronos became the Sahajiya in 1825, then the Cultists of Bacchus, then the Cult of Ecstasy.

items.title: Don Sebastian
items.text: Don Sebastian was a Californio landowner who sheltered the survivors of the brig Danube, wrecked in San Pedro Bay on Christmas Day 1828.

items.title: The Storm Eater’s escape
items.text: It broke free some time in the 1830s, as caern after caern fell to the European Garou, and the Garou needed decades even to learn its name.

items.title: The Storm Eater reborn
items.text: In the 1830s the Europeans’ seizure of too many Uktena and Wendigo caerns weakened the seals, and the Bane slipped out and began feeding again.

items.title: Mage history from 1756
items.text: Babbage and Lovelace's work in 1834 gave rise to the Difference Engineers, who became the Virtual Adepts around 1880; the Natural Philosophers renamed themselves Electrodyne Engineers in 1866.

items.title: Seneschal
items.text: Princes cite the Nuremberg affair of 1836, when a Sabbat spy became seneschal and passed what was learned to the sect.

items.title: Archbishop Strathcona
items.text: In the years before the Rebellions of 1837 and 1838, Strathcona watched the city's cliquish ancillae, likened to an old boys' club, spend their nights on their wealth at the Beaver Club and the Exchange Coffee House, and judged it time for the Sabbat to act.

items.title: The Gothic Victorian Age
items.text: Victoria has ruled the Empire's living subjects since 1837, so few alive remember any other reign.

items.title: Montreal (Sabbat city)
items.text: In an 1838 letter to Prince Mithras of London, Archbishop Strathcona claimed that Montreal had always belonged to the Sabbat and warned the Camarilla off, calling it the City of Black Miracles.

items.title: Archbishop Strathcona
items.text: Strathcona wrote to Prince Mithras of London in April 1838, declaring that once-friends were now dead to each other and that Montreal would be defended against the Camarilla.

items.title: San Francisco in the Gold Rush
items.text: In 1849 San Francisco grew from 900 people to 26,000, with another 100,000 passing through on the way to the hills.

items.title: Darklings in the occult revival
items.text: As the Order of Reason began turning into the Technocratic Union in the mid-1800s, several were caught in the fighting, and the survivors passed on a warning to stay out of wizards' affairs.

ruling.note: The Technocracy's birth: Book of Shadows (2nd) says the Order of Reason became the Technocratic Union in the mid-1800s; M20 p. 27 says the Order of Reason lasted until 1897. Read as a change begun in the mid-1800s and finished in 1897; the card also moves from 1800 to 1850.

items.title: Financiers and the Proctor takeover
items.text: In 1851 the tangle of guild laws was folded into one body named the Financiers.

items.title: Alex Swift
items.text: A Virginian Confederate officer from 1861, friend to Stonewall Jackson, shot and left for dead at the Battle of Fisher's Hill.

items.title: Lady Margaret Willoughby
items.text: A Tremere of the 9th Generation, perhaps antitribu, Embraced in 1864; sire Lady Lise Paulmann is destroyed.

items.title: Badr al-Budur
items.text: An Assamite of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1867 by Ma'aruf, and of the same lineage as the notorious Fatima.

items.title: Miria, the Bygone Visions Caern
items.text: Shadow Lords have been barred from the island since their treachery in 1868, and Get of Fenris of both sexes since 1967, when Get women seeking sanctuary opened a moon bridge for their kin to seize it.

items.title: Don Sebastian
items.text: From 25 December 1870 Don Sebastian governed Los Angeles as prince, a stern but fair ruler to the refugees who came south from San Francisco, caring nothing for their pasts so long as they kept the rules of the domain.
items.ref: Los Angeles by Night p. 21 (pdf 22); Los Angeles by Night p. 22 (pdf 23)

items.title: The Giovanni of New York
items.text: Through paid dispatchers, customs men and dock and ground crews, the Giovanni have watched what moves up the Hudson since the 1870s and through Idlewild, now Kennedy, airport since 1962.

items.title: New York
items.text: Tammany Hall, run by Boss Tweed, keeps great power through illegal favours and vote-gathering, despite a setback in the 1870s.

items.title: Devil's Night (1871)
items.text: A suicidal Malkavian lit the flames that swept the city in 1871. Few mortals died, but some 18,000 buildings burned and Maxwell's supporters were nearly all destroyed.

items.title: Kingston, Ontario
items.text: Prince Iain MacLaren, a ninth-generation Ventrue banker Embraced in London in 1874, took the city after leaving Britain in 1979; a paid arrangement with Lucian of Gary to move Kindred down the river into the States funds the post.

items.title: Black Eagle Consulting
items.text: It began in 1877 amid Sabbat raids on Midwestern telegraph stations, when a templar saw that fast communication could offset the Camarilla's social reach.

items.title: New Orleans After Reconstruction
items.text: The end of Reconstruction in 1877 eased the city's burdens but left behind a group of Kindred from the North who had tasted power there and want more.

items.title: Lodin
items.text: Lodin ruled through money and force, using police and private guards to keep the workers in line, until strikes and Modius's rebellion shook that rule in the 1880s.

items.title: The Gothic Victorian Age
items.text: For the game the age runs almost two decades, from 1880 to 1897.

items.title: The Kindred and the Occult Revival
items.text: Mortals start the Golden Dawn in 1880, but Kindred soon infest it and use it to draw living initiates.

items.title: Founding of the Arcanum
items.text: Holmscroft wrote the society's rituals, first held at Christmas 1885; a founder suspected they were far older than the Arcanum.

items.title: Conclave
items.text: The Minneapolis conclave of 1887 tried Prince Cyril Ximenes for tyranny over the Masquerade.

items.title: Salvatore Giovanni
items.text: A Giovanni of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1887 by Rosario Giovanni.

items.title: The Fall of the Storm Eater
items.text: The Storm Eater, a blend of Weaver and Wyrm, was destroyed in 1889 by a rite the Pure Ones and Wyrmcomers found together; the Wendigo say its exact form is now lost.

items.title: The Ninth Wave
items.text: Founded in 1890 and named after a Tennyson poem, it holds that the Antediluvians sleep for lack of magic and will wake when a second Flood of magic comes.

items.title: Salvador Garcia
items.text: Salvador Garcia is a Brujah, sired by Ferdinand and Embraced in 1892, who looks about 23.

items.title: The Computer
items.text: In 1895 the Artificers moved their best difference engine to Autochthonia, where power was plentiful and no Sleeper could see it.

items.title: The Order of Reason becomes the Technocratic Union
items.text: The Order of Reason reorganizes as the Technocracy.

ruling.note: Kept at 1897 (M20 p. 27), the date the other Mage cards are fitted to.

items.title: The Computer
items.text: The common account says the engine reached full sentience in 1897 on the tenth iteration of a new algorithm, and the Machinists renamed their Convention Iteration X.

items.title: Dracula in London
items.text: In 1897 Vlad Dracula arrives in London and whispers a story to an Irish author that strains the Masquerade to its limits.

items.title: The Groundskeepers
items.text: A militant offshoot founded in 1898, the Master Edenic Groundskeepers, wants to strike first; it has drifted from the main body since the 1960s and may soon break away.
items.ref: War of Ages p. 74 (pdf 75); War of Ages p. 75 (pdf 76)

items.title: The War of Tears ends
items.text: The Bunyip are hunted out as Europeans settle Australia. No living Bunyip remains.

items.title: Kyoko Shinsegawa
items.text: A warrior and linguist who came to California around 1900 and served the Prince of San Francisco against the Sabbat and lawless Anarchs.

items.title: Spiritualism in the West
items.text: Even the Luciferian Movement, Satanism included, became widespread by the 1900s.

items.title: Seats won and lost
items.text: The Sons of Ether left the Technocracy in 1905 and took the empty Seat once held by the Solificati in 1906; in 1932 the Ahl-i-Batin quit the Council over Middle Eastern Quintessence.

items.title: Las Vegas, city of control
items.text: The city was formally founded in 1905, and federal interest in the area began with surveys ahead of the Hoover Dam.

items.title: The Utopian League
items.text: A 1905 symposium across Europe set down the Scientific Ethos, with the League charged to ease Etherite work into the Consensus.

items.title: Kyoko Shinsegawa
items.text: The 1906 earthquake woke the torpid Nosferatu elder Fa Chen Leong amid the fires, who attacked believing assassins had come.

items.title: Dr. Paulinus Mercer
items.text: In 1907 Mercer played while the Ecstatic dancer Isadora Duncan performed in Paris; witnesses saw the hall flicker into a Greek temple and the light of Olympus, and some of the crowd went mad or rioted.

items.title: Lodin and Modius in Chicago
items.text: In 1908 Lodin warned the city's oldest Kindred that anarch actions threatened the Masquerade, and the elders allowed Lodin to end the conflict by any means.

items.title: Adventurers
items.text: The name was first pinned on Mathieu Hullebusch in 1909 for a flying-automaton bid to overthrow the colonial rulers of the Belgian Congo.

items.title: Cybernetic Research Institute
items.text: Former Electrodyne Engineers formed it in 1910, aiming to share research so the Masses could build their prototypes and so steal assembly-line power from the Union.

items.title: Lodin and Modius in Chicago
items.text: By 1913 Lodin held the city and Modius fled.

items.title: Mage history from 1756
items.text: Stopping Lord Vargo in 1914 led to the New World Order's founding; the Ahl-i-Batin left the Council in 1932; a short alliance with the Union beat back the Nephandi in the Second World War.

items.title: Dr. Douglas Netchurch
items.text: A Malkavian of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1915 by Trimeggian, born into wealth.

items.title: The Fourth Great Maelstrom
items.text: The dead of the Great War flood the Underworld. The Somme sets off a storm that ravages the Shadowlands.
items.ref: Wraith 20th p. 39 (pdf 104); Wraith: The Great War pdf 34, 206

items.title: The Underworld after the Armistice
items.text: The setting covers the years from Armistice Day, 11 November 1918, up to the night before the stock market crash of 1929.

items.title: The Louisiana Technomancers
items.text: In the 1920s and 1930s Doran learned of a Syndicate of mages in southern Louisiana. Huey Long worked with other Technomancers in the north of the state and was killed by yet another group of mages.

items.title: Karen Anatos
items.text: Once Lily Thorne, an American silent film actress who fell into a river while filming in the Black Forest in the late 1920s and was Embraced underwater by the Gangrel Methuselah Brunhilde.

items.title: Psychic Groups
items.text: Insight Investments is a fast-growing Chicago investment house; the Marsh Institute goes back to a telepathic financier who made a fortune in 1920s real estate and was warned of the crash by a precognitive rival.

items.title: The Giovanni of New York
items.text: The clan's ties to the Gambino crime family go back to 1921, when the Giovanni supplied Joe Masseria with fresh talent for a cut of the racket.

items.title: The Scroll of Thothmes
items.text: In 1923 Professor Donald Richardson claimed that a relic from the reign of Thothmes I described a secret society of Sacred Artisans, writing in a script only the Enlightened could read.

items.title: Akhu
items.text: In 1930 the Council of Seven forbade any study of Akhu, then allowed it again in 1973, persuaded by the Pontifex of Antioch, who argued the clan had to know the Serpents' magic to defend against it.

items.title: Wu Lung
items.text: The Technocracy, the Japanese invasion of the 1930s and Communist rule have left the Wu Lung greatly weakened.

items.title: Dylan Bruce
items.text: A Scot who dug shelters in London in the late 1930s for the Ventrue Gotsdam, who had the family build fortified havens across England and later sent Dylan to France with the British Expeditionary Force.

items.title: FBI Special Affairs Department
items.text: The Special Affairs Department is thought to date from the end of the Truman years, but its roots go back to the 1930s.

items.title: The Anacreon revolts
items.text: In 1931 an Anacreon of the Silent Legion in Boston resigned, protesting that Stygia ignored the Shadowlands beyond its borders while the mortal crisis stretched local Legions past their limits.

ruling.note: Kept: the 1931 resignation comes before Charon is lost in 1945 (ev-fifth-great-maelstrom); the Necropoli drift away after that. The Encyclopaedia date now says so.

items.title: The Flesh Court of Shanghai
items.text: Since Japan invaded China in 1937, Shanghai and the provinces under the Flesh Court have fought a nightly war against Japanese akuma, and its rule has decayed into a loose oligarchy.

items.title: Dylan
items.text: On the night of October 10, 1940, bombs fell across more than 50 districts of London, while Dylan Bee sheltered in a trench by the Thames.

items.title: The Zoot-Suit Riots (1943)
items.text: In June 1943 ghouls of Don Sebastian drove into Venice and beat up anarchs who had fled the Mexican Sabbat; the police arrested the victims. The anarchs struck back at the Don's thugs the next night.

items.title: Dr. Vermundo de Sancha
items.text: A Tzimisce of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1943 by Efrain Sortano, once a medical professor.

items.title: The Second Anarch Revolt
items.text: Anarchs drive the Camarilla out of California and declare the Anarch Free State.

items.title: The Free State's later years
items.text: Don Sebastian had Jeremy MacNeil seized and beaten in 1944. MacNeil urged six weeks of patience, and on 21 December 1944 armed anarchs struck the elders in their havens before dawn.

items.title: Anarch Free States (California)
items.text: By the end of the Revolt's second night every Los Angeles elder had been destroyed, driven off or forced into hiding, and just before dawn on 22 December 1944 Jeremy MacNeil proclaimed the Anarch Free States.

items.title: Status Perfectus
items.text: The Revolutionary Council, the leaders of the 1944 Revolt, wrote the Status Perfectus, the 'Perfect State', setting out how the Free States would govern themselves rather than be ruled.

items.title: The Fifth Great Maelstrom
items.text: The bombs tear the Tempest open. Gorool rises, and Charon is lost fighting it.

items.title: Anarch Free States (California)
items.text: By the end of February 1945 the Free States ran from the Mexican border north to San Jose, and from the Pacific to within 50 miles of Nevada.

items.title: Abandoned Labyrinths
items.text: Most Nephandi were driven past the Horizon in 1945, leaving centuries of building behind; a few strongholds were found and burned, but most never were.

items.title: Seats won and lost
items.text: A short wartime alliance with the Technocracy crushed a rising Nephandi threat and was disowned in 1946, when the Council marked its renewal with Reconciliation Day.

items.title: Mage history from 1756
items.text: A spacecraft crashed near Roswell in 1947, hidden by the Void Engineers and New World Order.

ruling.note: Iteration X's name: Mage Storyteller's Companion (2nd) says the end of the 1950s, Convention Book: Iteration X (Revised) says 1897, and M20 counts Iteration X from about 1900. 1897 stands; the 1950s clause is cut.

items.title: The Triads
items.text: Hong Kong was the Triad capital from 1949 until the 1997 handover, which sent many societies overseas and drew Western attention to them for the first time; their roots lie in old Chinese secret societies.

items.title: The Unmastered
items.text: Four founders (Philip Marshall, Enrico Sagunto, Ginerva Salamanca and Gregory Winter) started it in the 1950s to help ghouls who escaped or were abandoned by their domitors.

items.title: The Panders
items.text: They rose after the Sabbat civil war of the late 1950s, when the clanless Joseph Pander led them against the Moderates at the urging of Lasombra and Tzimisce elders, and won formal recognition.

items.title: Victor the Assassin
items.text: A Tremere of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1950 by Duke Traska; a decorated Second World War soldier who later worked for an unnamed intelligence agency.

items.title: John Eaton Simcoe
items.text: In the 1950s Simcoe and other Syndicate members formed the Dominion Gaming Group, later DCG Ltd.

items.title: The Order of St. Michael
items.text: Founded in the 1950s among early liberation theologians of Central America, it sets out to bring justice and mercy to those denied both.

items.title: New York (Kindred city)
items.text: By one Sabbat veteran's count, New York in the late 1950s held perhaps 300 Cainites, half of them Lasombra and Tzimisce.

items.title: Genegineers in the 1990s
items.text: Genegineers were called Mutagenic Engineers until 1954.

items.title: Sullivan Dane
items.text: Born in England in 1957, Dane felt called to the Lord's work young and sought to join the Jesuits in 1980.

items.title: Conclave
items.text: Any Kindred who hears the call may attend, and young vampires may speak. In 1957 a switch of venue from Rotterdam to Brussels left visiting American elders to walk into the Sabbat.
items.ref: Guide to the Camarilla p. 131 (pdf 132); Guide to the Camarilla p. 132 (pdf 133)

items.title: Carolina Valez
items.text: A Lasombra of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1957 by Tobias Smith as part of a Sabbat campaign.

items.title: The Mariana Trench
items.text: The Mariana Trench, the deepest point of the planet's surface, holds the ocean's strongest Grotto; Void Engineer explorers first reached it in 1960, and a few squads and two Tradition cabals have gone down since.

items.title: Chicago (Kindred city)
items.text: As the largest Camarilla city in the United States, Chicago turned into the main battleground of the 1960s War of Ages against the anarchs.

items.title: Fishin'
items.text: A pestilent, ratlike creature that the Sabbat take for a werewolf has been seen in the city's sewers since the 1960s. To lure it out, packs lower mortal bait on a rope into the sewers, and something below always kills it.

items.title: The Patient Deed
items.text: Many of the Patient Deed stood down when True Silverheels called for the camps to end, remembering protests of the 1960s that had gone badly.

items.title: The Free State's later years
items.text: The Free State survived a Sabbat attack in 1965 and a war with a mortal gang in 1992, but the Cathayan invasion of 1998 broke it. Anarchs briefly held San Francisco before Cathayans drove them out in mid-1998.

items.title: Angelo, the Blood Brother
items.text: During the 1966 riots in Los Angeles, after the Sabbat siege of the city, a nomad Sabbat pack watched a mortal gang led by a young drug-fuelled man named Angelo burn building after building.

items.title: Lodin
items.text: After the anarchs were crushed in 1968, Lodin outlawed the Embrace across the metropolitan area, and for the most part the ban was obeyed.

items.title: The Night of Rage
items.text: The war ended at the 1968 Democratic convention. With the Ventrue justicar's leave, Lodin sent police and elders against the protesters, and archons and elders fell on the anarchs out of sight of the cameras. More than 100 vampires vanished that night.
items.ref: Chicago by Night p. 22 (pdf 23); Chicago by Night p. 23 (pdf 24)

items.title: The Bamboo Princes
items.text: The name Takeouji comes from a 1968 manifesto by Burakumin, which called the old ways hopelessly outdated and asked for a new breed of Kuei-jin with all the virtues of bamboo.

items.title: The Resurgence
items.text: As people watch the first steps on the Moon, Dreaming floods back into the world and some of the lost fae return.

items.title: Arcadia
items.text: Sidhe came back out of Arcadia at the Resurgence, when the gates opened again in 1969.

items.title: The Resurgence
items.text: The gates to Arcadia opened again on July 20, 1969.

items.title: Autumn Sidhe
items.text: Liam and Scathach nobles took the Changeling Way rather than flee, and greeted the returning sidhe in 1969.

items.title: Ailil and the right of demesne
items.text: When the noble houses returned in 1969, Seelie houses seized every freehold they could and drove out the commoners who had kept them; Ailil says many of those freeholds were once its own and refuses to honor the new holders.

items.title: Star Council
items.text: In 1969 the group broke into a restricted hangar, and it keeps the devices it found hidden in abandoned warehouses.

items.title: Azrael (Svein Fortinbras)
items.text: Born in Bergen in 1970, Svein rose in the Norwegian black metal scene of the early 1990s and was Embraced in 1991 by Brynjar, a Follower of Set of the 12th Generation.

items.title: Edgardo Robbia
items.text: Edgardo took work from mortals and Kindred alike, and in the 1970s grew close to the Baader-Meinhof Group.

items.title: Ian MacLaren
items.text: After a string of financial mistakes in the 1970s, MacLaren was urged to leave and became Prince of Kingston, Ontario.

items.title: The Zaibatsu and the Elemental Dragons
items.text: Other Asian Technocratic bodies kept silent too; in the late 1970s a few Taiping Tianguo agents admitted aiding North Vietnamese forces on Syndicate orders.

items.title: Cybernetic Research Institute
items.text: The Institute was never just about computers, though its close work with the Virtual Adepts through the 1970s and 1980s led many to think so.

items.title: Vancouver, a Haven City
items.text: Several old vampires gained sway over major local businesses, including forestry firms, while Richard Daly, a rich and influential businessman who leads the Glass Walkers, became a key figure of Garou Vancouver from the early 1970s.

items.title: Highgate Cemetery
items.text: Opened in the mid-19th century, Highgate has always had ties to the supernatural, including talk of a Vampire of Highgate in the 1970s and 1980s.

items.title: Black Tooth
items.text: Black Tooth, a Simba from Zululand, gathered a pride in the ivory wars of the late 1970s and struck at all European intruders, supernatural or mundane.

items.title: Track 6A
items.text: While building Atlanta's subway in the late 1970s, MARTA crews failed again and again to blast through one stretch of granite that geologists could find nothing wrong with.

items.title: Madame Yacine
items.text: In 1974 the French Tremere won over Madame Yacine, a Malkavian practitioner living among the Algerian community of Lyon.

items.title: Colm Olliver
items.text: A Brujah of the 11th Generation, Embraced in 1974 by Fat Ciaran; ambushed and staked on a farm truck bound for London in 1976, then left in torpor three years.

items.title: Varosha
items.text: Cordoned off since the Turkish invasion of 1974, Varosha is frozen in time, its shops still hung with clothes untouched for decades.

items.title: The Batini and Iran
items.text: Training of new Qutbs began in Isfahan in October 1979.

items.title: The Reprieve of 1979
items.text: In 1979 the Shah's government fell and Technocratic agents were driven out of Iran, a turn the Batini call the Reprieve.

items.title: Maria DiMatto
items.text: DiMatto, child of a Giovanni cousin, was Embraced in 1980 after a youthful fascination with the darker side of the family.

items.title: Atlantic City
items.text: Few Restless gathered in Atlantic City until gambling was made legal there in 1980; before that its dead were mostly Enfants and old wraiths bound to happier summers, ignored by Hierarchy and Heretic alike.

items.title: Sullivan Dane
items.text: In 1982 Dane destroyed a neonate in Washington, D.C., and in that moment was flooded with names, faces and scenes, sure of a calling to hunt vampires.

items.title: The Russian Silence
items.text: In 1985 the Council sought a normal footing with the Camarilla against unnamed threats; in 1990 all contact stopped, then all contact with any Kindred in Russia, and Tremere spying there failed.

items.title: The Mexico City earthquake of 1985
items.text: The quake of 19 September 1985 damaged over 4,000 buildings and killed more than 9,000 people.

items.title: Lodin
items.text: In 1986, in return for Annabelle's support against the anarch leader Maldavis, Lodin had to let Annabelle make two childer and to attend the primogen in Elysium on the first Monday of every month.

items.title: Chicago primogen
items.text: Procet, a member of the council, vanished in the Thanksgiving Massacre of 1986, when Lodin's mortal servants staked anarchs in their havens by day.
items.ref: Chicago by Night p. 24 (pdf 25); Chicago by Night p. 25 (pdf 26)

items.title: The House of Storms
items.text: Its resident, Kathryn Green, made a fortune in the 1987 stock market crash by buying while others sold.

items.title: Baba Yaga and the Fall of the Wall
items.text: Even Gustav was caught off guard when the crossing points opened on November 9, 1989; hoping to win back lost ground, the prince let the Wall come down from June 13, 1990.

items.title: Meixiu
items.text: A Malkavian of the 10th Generation, Embraced in 1989 by Colin McAllister; each night the delusion of being the Black Dragon Princess, heir of the Yellow Emperor, grows stronger.

items.title: Jaromir Cerny
items.text: Old Clan Tzimisce of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1989 by Janek Ritka; dissident parents were arrested in Prague under Gustav Husak.

name: Modern and the Time of Judgment

items.title: The Russian Silence
items.text: With Soviet money gone, Anarchs in Latin America and Africa lost heavily through the 1990s.

items.title: Baba Yaga and the Fall of the Wall
items.text: Baba Yaga stirred from torpor in 1990 and set out to bring the eastern lands back under the Nosferatu elder's control.

items.title: The Locksmiths
items.text: The Locksmiths began in the late 1990s, founded by a Glass Walker called only Strangelove, as a network for Glass Walker Kinfolk.

items.title: The Shadow Curtain
items.text: When the Baba Yaga rose and the Shadow Curtain fell in the early 1990s, supernatural Russia disappeared behind an invisible barrier.

items.title: The Succubus Club
items.text: The first club opened in Chicago in the early 1990s, where Kindred fed on mortals drawn to the vampire scene; tonight it is a nomadic party moving across North America.

ruling.note: Kept as the club's opening; placed at 1991 so it comes before the 1993 Lupine attack on it.

items.title: The Russian Silence
items.text: From 1991 four archon teams went in, the last with a former Justicar, and none returned; the Camarilla now leaves Russia alone and hopes whatever is there stays put.

items.title: Lula Birch
items.text: A Gangrel antitribu of the Twelfth Generation, Embraced in 1991 by Pedro Diaz, raised in Arkansas farm country.

items.title: Lodin's Boardroom
items.text: In 1993 Prince Lodin called a Blood Hunt on the werewolves and died in the Lupine rampage, along with half the city's Kindred.

ruling.note: Lodin's death: V20 Companion says the mid-1990s and half the city's Kindred; Chicago by Night (2nd) dates the attack to 1993 and its entry says a third. The year 1993 fits both; the toll follows V20.

items.title: The werewolf war of 1993
items.text: On a moonlit night in 1993, werewolves struck the heart of the city, aiming at the Succubus Club. Lodin called a Blood Hunt on the Lupines.

ruling.note: Kept: the 1993 attack on the Succubus Club. Lodin's death and the toll are on en-v20c-lodins-boardroom-0.

items.title: Ayisha Jocastian
items.text: A letter of Ayisha's travels, on Giovanni and Setite influence, appeared in the 1993 edition of the ancient Noddist scripture compiled by Aristotle de Laurent and Beckett.

items.title: Conclave
items.text: Conclaves meet for grave matters, trials of mighty Kindred or the removal of corrupt princes, and they often rule on the Traditions. The 1994 conclave took up the Internet and the Masquerade.

items.title: The Montreal archdiocese
items.text: In 1994 Ezekiel, childe of Sangris, returned at the head of a Black Hand pack to claim the seat, and the Shepherds put forward the former inquisitor Alfred Benezri. Each of the city's covens has lined up behind one of the three.

items.title: Pentex’s corporate history
items.text: Its later directors include Harold Zettler and Executive Vice President Peter Culliford, whose combined experience is said to span more than a thousand years; Culliford reorganised the Board into its present subdivisions in 1994.
items.ref: W20 Pentex Handbook p. 5 (pdf 6); Subsidiaries p. 11 (pdf 12)

items.title: ShreckNet
items.text: ShreckNet began as a joke name for secret Nosferatu hubs on the early military network; privatisation in 1995 and the boom in hubs shrank it to a vampire-only net across about thirty cities.

items.title: The fall of the College on Mus
items.text: In August 1995 a Technocratic fleet attacked the Chantry; a third force of Umbrood, wormlike beasts and Nephandi then struck both sides and took the College.

items.title: The Martian Penumbra
items.text: Two Tradition settlements stand where seven canals meet, the Trivium Charontis: the terraformed grounds of Doissetep, whose great house sits in an overlap zone with the Shade Realm of Forces, and a Sons of Ether camp nicknamed Bradbury, set up with the Deacons' leave in summer 1996.

items.title: The fall of Doissetep
items.text: The Hermetic stronghold destroys itself. The Digital Web crashes in the Great Whiteout.

items.title: Bone Flowers in Hong Kong
items.text: That uneasy peace fell apart in 1997, when the Quincunx resolved to seize Hong Kong from the Kin-jin by force.

items.title: The Pogrom
items.text: In 1997 a cabal tried to bring down a Horizon Construct, setting off days of slaughter on the Front Lines.

items.title: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe
items.text: Ratkin Tunnel Runners riddled the Shadow Curtain over Asia with boltholes, and when it fell in late 1998 the local wererats claimed the credit.

items.title: The Breaking
items.text: Until late 1998 every Assamite carried the Tremere curse: vampire blood harmed them and gave no nourishment, and attempted diablerie burned them with no gain.

items.title: Baba Yaga
items.text: In 1998 Lupines slew Baba Yaga. The Shadow Curtain fell, and Russian Nosferatu now hide as autarkis between the Camarilla to the west and Cathayans eager for the old domains to the east.

items.title: Justicars
items.text: Since the Gangrel left the sect, there has been no Gangrel justicar; Xaviar was the last. By the 1998 meeting most of the justicars were new appointees.

items.title: The death of the Baba Yaga
items.text: Through 1998 the Garou dismantled the Baba Yaga’s power piece by piece, and that obsession with the werewolves may have left the sorceress open to vampire foes.

items.title: The Fallen escape the Abyss
items.text: Fallen angels slip out of their prison and take the bodies of the dying.

items.title: The Reckoning
items.text: The first of the imbued see the world as it is. From now on hunters follow Hunter: The Reckoning.
items.ref: Hunter: The Reckoning pp. 26-38 (pdf 27-39), the opening journal, dated October 1999

items.title: The Sixth Great Maelstrom
items.text: The greatest storm of all scours the Underworld. In its chaos the Abyss cracks and the mummies' souls are torn loose.
items.ref: Wraith: The Oblivion, Ends of Empire (2nd edition). Wraith 20th p. 213 (pdf 278) treats it as not yet come.

items.title: The Avatar Storm
items.text: A storm in the spirit world flays the souls of mages who try to cross the Gauntlet.

items.title: The Week of Nightmares
items.text: A week of mass nightmares and visions as something ancient wakes and rampages across India and Bangladesh.

items.title: ShreckNet
items.text: After a 1999 scare over a bulletin board for monster hunters, the Camarilla set up a task force to watch the Internet; it now uses scores of vampires and thousands of servants and is still too small.

items.title: The naraka
items.text: In the summer of 1999 the Dreaming around Bangladesh was almost wiped out by fire; the naraka emerged into the Autumn World from that wasteland, the first thing they saw being Kali the destroyer, whom they took as mother.

items.title: Research & Execution
items.text: R&E repairs gear and vessels and runs labs; 32.7% of its people stay home, down from about 55% before 1999.

items.title: The Dimensional Anomaly
items.text: The Anomaly struck at the end of June 1999, tearing across the Spatial Horizon like a hurricane with reality at its eye.

items.title: Vitel and Garlotte
items.text: Marcus Vitel became prince of Washington some thirty years before 1999, when the previous prince, Marissa of Clan Tremere, met an end; Garlotte, prince of nearby Baltimore, has been a rival ever since and took Vitel in after Washington fell.
items.ref: Clan Novel Saga 2 p. 5 (pdf 7); Clan Novel Saga 2 p. 29 (pdf 31); Beckett p. 59 (pdf 60)

items.title: The generals of the 1999 Sabbat war
items.text: The Sabbat offensive begun in mid-June 1999 took Atlanta, Washington and most cities between; three archbishops led it: Sascha Vykos (newly made archbishop in Washington), Borges (of Miami) and Francisco Polonia (of New York).
items.ref: Clan Novel Saga 3 p. 5 (pdf 7); Beckett p. 59 (pdf 60)

items.title: The strike on Monçada
items.text: In September 1999 Lucita went to Madrid, where the Cardinal Monçada kept a haven beneath the church of San Nicolás de las Servitas, while the Assamite Fatima gathered word of its defences.
items.ref: Clan Novel Saga 4 p. 16 (pdf 18); Clan Novel Saga 4 p. 18 (pdf 20); Clan Novel Saga 4 p. 31 (pdf 33); CB Lasombra (Rev) p. 97 (pdf 92)

items.title: The Cyber Dogs
items.text: At the end of 1999, Elizabeth Genereader of the Random Interrupts told the tribe by video link that the Cyber Dogs had experimented on unwilling lupus Garou.

items.title: ShreckNet
items.text: After a Malkavian blogger's breach in 2000 many elders banned it, which in effect gave the Internet to the Anarchs and angered young Kindred of every sect.

items.title: The Eldest and the du'at
items.text: The du'at was the council of the three caste heads: the Caliph of the warriors, the Vizier of the viziers and the Amr of the sorcerers. Alamut's records date it to around 2000 BC.

items.title: The Assamite Schism
items.text: Schismatics first appeared publicly in early 2000. They read Haqim's Law of Judgement with moderation and call the slaughter of all other vampires genocide.

items.title: The Dimensional Anomaly
items.text: It began to ease by New Year's Day 2000 and lessened again by autumn 2000, yet it never fully ended.

items.title: Fangster
items.text: In 2001 a coterie of Tremere defectors brought Technomancy lore to the Free States and, backed by the Red Question, released free programs with ritual effects built in, usable without any knowledge of Thaumaturgy.

items.title: The Evanescence
items.text: The Evanescence is dated to around September 11, 2001.

items.title: The Time of Judgment
items.text: The end the lines foretold. Each line's ending is the Storyteller's to choose, or to skip.
items.ref: Era table: Time of Judgment (house rule switch)

items.title: The Bhuvar
items.text: Disasters in the living world of India, such as the 2004 tsunami and the yearly monsoon floods, echo as dangers in the Bhuvar, the realm of the dead beside it.

ruling.note: The tsunami of December 2004 falls after the Time of Judgment year. It stands only when the Storyteller skips the Time of Judgment endings, like every classic event after 2004.
